current_events: Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi and Omani foreign minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi say that Iran and Oman have discussed a proposal to establish a temporary joint shipping route for ships in the Strait of Hormuz
United States president Donald Trump and the country's navy say that all mines have been cleared from the Strait of Hormuz
2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reports that a oil tanker has been struck by a unknown projectile off the coast of Oman near the strait. No casualties are reported
The Wall Street Journal reports that U.S. president Trump launched Operation Epic Fury in February despite warnings from U.S. vice president JD Vance and then-intelligence director Tulsi Gabbard
The Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces announce they have officially dissolved and completed a merger with the Syrian army following the end of the civil war in 2024
Aftermath of the Syrian civil war
The Israel Defense Forces and Shin Bet says that they have struck five Hamas weapons storage systems and a launch site in Gaza including in mosques
Around 27 people, including four children, are reported to be killed by Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North (SPLM-N) militants in the South Kordofan areas of Kadugli and Abu Hitan
Sudan’s Ministry of Human Resources and Social Welfare reports that 224 cases of child sexual violence has been documented since the conflict
War crimes in the Sudanese civil war

The Australian Recording Industry Association bans wholly AI-generated music from appearing on its charts starting in September 2026. The ruling aims to distinguish fully AI-generated music and AI-assisted music, where the track is human-created but uses AI as a supporting tool
AI boom, Artificial intelligence in music
Canada announces retaliatory tariffs on about US$20 billion worth of U.S. annual imports in response to the 50% tariffs by U.S. president Donald Trump and his administration
2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico
Canada–United States relations
Latvia's cabinet ministry announces that the country will ban imported goods from Belarus and Russia starting September 1
Boycott of Russia and Belarus, Belarus–Latvia relations, Latvia–Russia relations
Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian war
South Korean automaker Hyundai Motor Company reaches a deal to end a month of walkouts by workers
At least 40 people are injured and over 300 homes are damaged in a tornado in Pomas, Occitania, France

Hungary foreign and deputy prime minister Anita Orbán files a criminal complaint against the government of former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán over its purchase of $965 million in ventilators during the COVID-19 pandemic in the country
